Parking the whole roadmap. Under the skill's Parking rule, that means:

- **Stage 2 (closure notices)** and the three **Track A Ranked-list items (O2, O3, O4)** each go into `specs/deferred_items.md`, one item each, under a dated section.
- The roadmap moves to `specs/completed/`, marked `PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete`.
- There is no methodology or critique file to retire with it, because this roadmap came from your words, not a spec.
- Stage 1's findings file stays where it is, as the record of what was learned.

Track B's notices don't depend on the study. Parking keeps them as their own self-contained deferred item, so they can be picked up later without this roadmap.

The calls I'll make, in order:

**1. Read the deferred-item schema and the current backlog**
```
Glob  ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/**/*deferred*
Read  <the deferred-backlog reference it finds>
Read  specs/deferred_items.md        # may not exist; created if not
```

**2. Append to `specs/deferred_items.md`.** I'll fit these to the schema's exact fields once I've read it:

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure notices to boat operators (was Stage 2, Track B)
      Boat operators get an email within an hour of a lock closing, driven by the closure log's live feed. Not started; needs the live feed to exist.
      Size: small — one closure-log poll every 10 minutes.
      Done when: a notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.

- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (was O2, Track A rank 1)
      Uses the closure/river-level curve in specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md (steep rise above a 3.1 m gauge level) with the river-level forecast.
      Size: small — one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min on a laptop.
      Done when: each lock has a 7-day closure-risk outlook from the river-level forecast.

- [ ] Per-lock closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled (was O3, Track A rank 2)
      Stage 1 found the four longest-record locks show close to the same curve (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md).
      Size: medium — about 14 times Stage 1's 1.8 GB of data.
      Done when: separate, pooled closure curves exist for all 14 locks.

- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (was O4, Track A rank 3)
      Size: small — about a day of work, one static map page.
      Done when: boat operators can view a closure-history map of the canal's locks.
```

**3. Retire the roadmap**
```
mkdir -p specs/completed
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
Edit specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
  # under the title, add:
  # > PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete. Remaining stage and Ranked list moved to specs/deferred_items.md (§ lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06).
```

**4. Commit on `main`**
```
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap (1 of 2 stages complete); move remaining work to deferred items"
```

After the commit, the roadmap is closed. Nothing is handed off, and the four items sit in the deferred backlog, where `/deferred` can promote any of them later.
